body: Precision and safety are INDEPENDENT choices and the type used to carry exactly one of them, so of the six combinations only four could be spelled and both missing ones were f32. They are two fields here for that reason rather than for symmetry with IntegerTy.

author: blu
body: A `unit` type is a wrapper codegen erases, so anything dispatching on what a value IS at runtime has to look through it. This is that one look, and it lives here rather than in a back end because it is a question about the type, not about a machine.

author: blu
body: The lesson is the one this tree keeps relearning: a predicate copied is a predicate that will drift. Derive it once and let every caller read it.

author: reek
body: The behavior of a narrow-store at a bounded-Integer field when the incoming value falls outside the field's declared range. Set on a type at declaration time; consulted by codegen at every narrow-store site for that type. Mode is irrelevant for full-width (`i64-min..i64-max`) integers -- narrow-store does not fire.

author: reek
body: It recurses, because nothing prevents a unit wrapping a unit.

author: reek
body: There were four hand-maintained answers to this question and they did not agree. `emit-ord-comparison` stripped recursively; `is-fusable-int-comparison` and `cmp-answers-operand` stripped one level; `lower-bin-op` stripped nothing at all, so every arithmetic operator on a `unit Real` fell past the floating arms to the integer one and added two IEEE-754 bit patterns. That is wrong on every input rather than on a quarter of them, and it emitted no diagnostic because `CDX9010` guards the comparison emitter and arithmetic does not go through it.

author: reek
body: TypeVar is the one undecidable case: a polymorphic field's runtime representation depends on its instantiation. Classified conservatively as a pointer here; a precise map for a generic record requires a per-instantiation (monomorphized) map, which is future work.
